Regional comparisons within the Danish healthcare system reveal significant variations in clinical practices, patient outcomes, and adherence to specific quality indicators across the country's five administrative regions. Analyzing data from the national clinical databases highlights how [[Danmark]] performs as a whole versus regional disparities in [[Region Hovedstaden]], [[Region Midtjylland]], [[Region Nordjylland]], [[Region Sjælland]], and [[Region Syddanmark]].

One major area of comparison involves the administration of timely medical interventions and admission practices. For [[Indikator 1]], which tracks the proportion of patients receiving antibiotics within three hours of hospital arrival, regional performance varied substantially, ranging from 22.5% in Region Syddanmark to 44.6% in Region Midtjylland [^src2]. Similarly, the rate of intermediate admissions ([[Indikator 5]]) showed notable geographic differences, fluctuating between 17.2% in Region Nordjylland and 27.0% in Region Syddanmark [^src3]. Other clinical metrics also demonstrated wide regional spreads: [[Indikator 5y]] ranged from 9.0% in Region Nordjylland to 19.9% in Region Hovedstaden [^src5], while [[Indikator 7]] varied drastically from 6.8% in Region Nordjylland to 33.1% in Region Hovedstaden [^src4]. Furthermore, [[Indikator 8]] saw proportions ranging from 41.9% in Region Nordjylland to 56.8% in Region Syddanmark [^src7], and [[Indikator 10]] varied from 9.9% in Region Midtjylland to 14.1% in Region Nordjylland [^src1].

Beyond process indicators, regional comparisons are critical for evaluating patient outcomes, particularly mortality following acute surgical procedures. For patients with a [[charlson-score-1-2]], the national 30-day mortality rate in Danmark was 11.2% (122 out of 1,090 patients) [^src6]. However, this average masks significant regional disparities. Region Sjælland and Region Nordjylland recorded the highest mortality rates at 15.6% and 17.1%, respectively [^src6]. In contrast, Region Hovedstaden and Region Syddanmark reported lower mortality rates of 9.1% and 9.9%, respectively, while Region Midtjylland stood at 10.7% [^src6]. These outcome metrics underscore the importance of continuous regional benchmarking to identify areas requiring clinical improvement and resource allocation.

## Claims

**Source: AKDB_2023.pdf, pages 26-30**
- Regionalt varierede andelen for indikator 5y fra 9,0 % i Region Nordjylland til 19,9 % i Region Hovedstaden [^src1] (region-nordjylland, region-hovedstaden, indikator-5y)

**Source: AKDB_2023.pdf, pages 51-55**
- Regionalt varierede andelen fra 9,9 % i Region Midtjylland til 14,1 % i Region Nordjylland for Indikator 10 [^src1] (region-midtjylland, region-nordjylland, indikator-10)

**Source: AKDB_2023.pdf, pages 61-65**
- Danmark: 122 / 1.090 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (11,2 %; 95 % CI: 9,4-13,2) [^src1] (danmark, charlson-score-1-2)
- Hovedstaden: 36 / 396 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (9,1 %; 95 % CI: 6,4-12,4) [^src1] (region-hovedstaden, charlson-score-1-2)
- Sjælland: 28 / 180 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (15,6 %; 95 % CI: 10,6-21,7) [^src1] (region-sjaelland, charlson-score-1-2)
- Syddanmark: 21 / 213 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (9,9 %; 95 % CI: 6,2-14,7) [^src1] (region-syddanmark, charlson-score-1-2)
- Midtjylland: 24 / 225 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (10,7 %; 95 % CI: 7,0-15,5) [^src1] (region-midtjylland, charlson-score-1-2)
- Nordjylland: 13 / 76 døde indenfor 30 dage efter akut kirurgi med Charlson Score = 1 eller 2 (17,1 %; 95 % CI: 9,4-27,5) [^src1] (region-nordjylland, charlson-score-1-2)

**Source: AKDB_2024.pdf, pages 11-15**
- Regionalt varierede andelen af patienter, der fik antibiotika indenfor tre timer efter ankomst til sygehus fra 22,5 % i Region Syddanmark til 44,6 % i Region Midtjylland [^src1] (region-syddanmark, region-midtjylland, indikator-1)

**Source: AKDB_2024.pdf, pages 31-35**
- Regionalt varierede andelen af intermediær indlæggelse fra 17,2 % i Region Nordjylland til 27,0 % i Region Syddanmark [^src1] (region-nordjylland, region-syddanmark, indikator-5)

**Source: AKDB_2024.pdf, pages 41-45**
- Regionalt varierede andelen fra 6,8 % i Region Nordjylland til 33,1 % i Region Hovedstaden [^src1] (indikator-7, region-nordjylland, region-hovedstaden)

**Source: AKDB_2024.pdf, pages 46-50**
- Regionalt varierede andelen fra 41,9 % i Region Nordjylland til 56,8 % i Region Syddanmark [^src1] (indikator-8, region-nordjylland, region-syddanmark)
